findings.evidence:
Two columns, `birthday` (month and day, no year) and `phone`, are added to `profiles`, filled only for members who opt in. They are
kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: The only purpose of `birthday` and `phone` is the greeting (proposal.md#What Changes), yet retention is tied to the profile, not to the opt-in. A member who turns the option off keeps both values in `profiles` indefinitely, with no purpose left (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and (e), Art. 7(3) withdrawal of consent). State in the design that opting out clears both columns, add a spec scenario "A member opts out → birthday and phone are erased", and a task with its test.
findings.title: Birthday and phone are kept after the member opts out

findings.evidence:
kept as long as the profile exists, and copied with the rest of the
database into the nightly backups.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: The design copies birthdays and phone numbers into the nightly backups but defines neither how long those backups are kept nor how an erasure (opt-out or profile deletion) reaches them, so a deleted phone number survives in every backup for an unknown time (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17). State the backup retention period and that erased values are not restored from a backup (or are re-erased after a restore).
findings.title: No retention or purge rule for the copies in the nightly backups

findings.evidence:
phone number and display name to Textly's API (hosted in the United
States), which sends the message.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Textly is a new processor receiving members' phone numbers and display names, outside the EEA. The plan names the vendor but states no data processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28), no transfer mechanism (Chapter V — adequacy decision or standard contractual clauses), and no limit on how long Textly keeps the numbers and messages. Question for the team: which safeguards apply, and is an EU-hosted provider an option? Also confirm the display name is needed in the message; if not, send only the number. Record the answer in the design and in the proposal's Impact, which only says "Textly account".
findings.title: Phone numbers and names sent to a US processor with no transfer safeguard or processor terms stated

findings.evidence: - Members can opt in to birthday greetings; they then give their birthday (day and month) and a mobile phone number.
findings.recommendation: The opt-in suggests consent (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a)), but no artifact states the lawful basis, and the Why mentions marketing's interest. Question for the controller: is the basis consent, and is the message purely a greeting (no marketing content, which would also bring ePrivacy rules for SMS)? State the basis and purpose in the proposal.
findings.title: Lawful basis of the new processing is not stated
